note: File: s3://pg-lineage-769063704696/results/rlneurons/r4/modal_t2-01/t2/T2.jsonl -> runs/theory-tests/T2.jsonl (500 rows, cap hits included), fields text, gold. Grading: the equivalence test behind score_v3, i.e. n13_score.grade(norm_v3(gold), norm_v3(candidate)) (math-verify, dollar_both wrapping); empty candidates count wrong; an exception from the grader counts wrong and is counted in grade_errors on the diagnostic line. Boxes come from rln4_lib._boxes (every '\boxed{' occurrence, nested ones too, unbalanced skipped; end = index after the matching brace). (b): case-insensitive 'answer is:?\s*' (no word boundary, so 'answer isn't' also matches; \s* may run over newlines); span ends at the first '\n' or '. ' after the match, or end of text; candidate end = span end. (c): matched line by line (case-sensitive 'Answer'), candidate end = end of the line. Cleaning: remove '$', '\(', '\)', '*', strip, drop one trailing '.', strip. 'A box inside a (b)/(c) span' = a box whose start lies inside the span; that (b)/(c) candidate is dropped and the box kept. Non-final = len(text) - end >= 800; flag = regex search in text[end:end+800]. Ambiguity, main (literal): when a (b) and a (c) candidate overlap each other (e.g. '**Answer:** The answer is 5'), both count. alt_measured: such overlapping (b)/(c) pairs count once, as the (b) span. Could shift the number: (c) candidates like 'is 5' from 'Answer is 5' grade wrong; repeated boxes of the same answer are pooled as separate candidates; the 800-char window may contain the next candidate. If there are no wrong or no right non-final candidates (r_R = 0), the ratio is undefined and the script reports not_computable.

Files: T2.jsonl (RL) as in k=1 and s3://pg-lineage-769063704696/results/rlneurons/r4/base_rl-02/out/T1.jsonl -> runs/theory-tests/T1.jsonl (base + cue), 500 rows each, cap hits included. Same extraction, grading, non-final filter and flag as k=1 (code identical). r_W, r_R pooled per file; a class with zero non-final candidates gets rate 0 as the recipe says. D = (r_W(T2) - r_W(T1)) - (r_R(T2) - r_R(T1)); refuted iff D > 0.18. alt_measured: overlapping (b)/(c) candidates counted once (as (b)). Both texts start with the stored ' line!' fragment; the text field is used as stored. Base T1 has more cap hits and loops: looping texts repeat boxes/answers many times, so pooled rates are dominated by a few long rows; nothing in the recipe weights rows, so none is applied.

Files: T2.jsonl and T1.jsonl as in k=2. Final score recomputed with rln4_lib.grade_v3(gold, text)['score_v3'] (the score_v3 procedure, not the stored v1/v2 'score'). Kept rows: score_v3 == 1 and cap_hit is False. A kept row counts 1 if it has at least one right non-final candidate (k=1 extraction, grading, >= 800 chars after its end) whose 800-char window matches the hold-on regex. F = mean over kept rows per file; statistic F(T2) - F(T1); refuted iff <= 0.0. alt_measured: overlapping (b)/(c) candidates counted once (as (b)); this can only change rows whose sole right flagged candidate is an overlapping (c) line. Note that longer texts have more chances to hold such a candidate, so differences in text length between models feed into the number. If a file had no kept rows the script reports not_computable.
